key_insight: A finite spanwise-oscillating wall reduced turbulent boundary-layer drag by 32%, with skin-friction onset and recovery decay lengths of 0.6δ and 0.9δ, respectively.
engineering_relevance: The measured response lengths can inform the placement and sizing of finite wall-actuation sections for turbulent drag control.
method: Investigate a turbulent boundary layer at Reτ = 652 with wall oscillations at T+ ≈ 101 and A+ ≈ 7.
Estimate local skin friction using arctangent-based nonlinear regression of near-wall data.
Track turbulence statistics and conditional quadrant events through control onset and recovery.
evidence_signal: The skin-friction estimator was assessed against reference DNS data and reproduced experimental measurement-error trends; most Reynolds-stress responses had exponential decay lengths within 0.5δ, except the slower shear-stress peak.
watch_item: The reported drag reduction does not establish net energy savings after accounting for wall-actuation power.
paper_title: Spatially developing drag reduction across a finite oscillating wall
